derivations.quote: Define the permutations $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ and $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$ (coordinate indices $j$, $k$ taken modulo $s$, $t$), which stay in the identity, never executed as sorts.
The other summands form $((N-I)u)_j$. The cited estimate gives $\|N-I\|<2.01e^{-\pi\alpha^2\theta/2}<2^{-\alpha^2\theta}$
Since $\alpha^2<p$ and $\theta>p/\alpha^4$, $\alpha^2\theta>p/\alpha^2>1$, so $\|N-I\|<1/2$ and $N$ is invertible by the Neumann series $N^{-1}=\sum_i(-1)^i(N-I)^i$.

Set $\mathsf S'=\mathsf S/2$, $\mathsf J'=N^{-1}/2$, $\mathsf D'=2^{-(2\alpha^2-2)}\mathsf D$, and put $A=\mathsf S'$ and $B_0=\mathsf D'\mathsf J'C$; these are contractions, since $\|C\|=1$ and the three factors have norms below $3/4$, $7/8$, $1$

As $C\mathsf T=N\mathsf D^{-1}$, the map $\mathsf DN^{-1}C$ is a left inverse of $\mathsf T$; applying it to the identity gives $\mathsf DN^{-1}CP_tF_t\mathsf S=P_sF_s$. The normalizations multiply to $2^{-(2\alpha^2-2)}2^{-1}2^{-1}=2^{-2\alpha^2}$, so $B_0P_tF_tA=2^{-2\alpha^2}P_sF_s$.

The cited algorithms give approximations $\widetilde{\mathsf S}'$, $\widetilde{\mathsf J}'$, $\widetilde{\mathsf D}'$ with errors $16p$, $3p^2/4$, $4$ and times $O(tp^{3/2+\delta}\alpha)$, $O(tp^{3/2+\delta}\alpha)$, $O(tp^{1+\delta})$
The selection $C$ picks an ordered subsequence (since $t/s>1$), and the indices are generated in order with $O(p)$ work each, so $C$ takes $O(tp)$ time with zero error

Take $\widetilde A=\widetilde{\mathsf S}'$ and $\widetilde B_0=\widetilde{\mathsf D}'\widetilde{\mathsf J}'C$. Contraction of the exact maps yields errors less than $16p<p^2$ and $4+3p^2/4<p^2$ (as $p>100$), and the costs add to $O(tp^{3/2+\delta}\alpha)$.
The Neumann series with $E=N-I$ and $k=\lceil p/(\alpha^2\theta)\rceil$ is evaluated as $\widetilde{\mathsf J}'u=\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}(-1)^j\widetilde v^{(j)}$ with every iterate kept in $\mathbb D_p$.

symbols.name: source length
symbols.meaning: The length of the prime-length Fourier transform being re-expressed.
symbols.quote: Gaussian resampling expresses a Fourier transform of length $s$ through one of a nearby larger length $t$ (a power of two there), so that only power-of-two transforms need a fast algorithm.

symbols.name: relative gap
symbols.meaning: The relative excess t/s-1 of the padded length over the source length.

symbols.name: input resampling
symbols.meaning: The Gaussian-weighted map from length-s to length-t complex vectors applied before the power-of-two transform.
symbols.quote: Harvey and van der Hoeven's maps $\mathsf S,\mathsf T$ from length-$s$ to length-$t$ complex vectors are, for $0\le k<t$, with $u$ extended periodically and $j$ over all integers,

symbols.name: output resampling
symbols.meaning: The Gaussian-weighted map from length-s to length-t complex vectors on the transform side of the identity.
symbols.quote: Harvey and van der Hoeven's maps $\mathsf S,\mathsf T$ from length-$s$ to length-$t$ complex vectors are, for $0\le k<t$, with $u$ extended periodically and $j$ over all integers,

symbols.name: nearest coordinate
symbols.meaning: The integer nearest tj/s, the coordinate of the length-t vector selected for index j.
symbols.quote: To undo $\mathsf T$, let $q_j$ be the integer nearest $tj/s$ and $\beta_j=tj/s-q_j$.

symbols.name: rounding offset
symbols.meaning: The difference tj/s-q_j between tj/s and its nearest integer.
symbols.quote: To undo $\mathsf T$, let $q_j$ be the integer nearest $tj/s$ and $\beta_j=tj/s-q_j$.

symbols.name: selection map
symbols.meaning: The map from length-t to length-s vectors that picks coordinate q_j for each j.
symbols.quote: Let $C$ select coordinates from length-$t$ to length-$s$ vectors, $(Cv)_j=v_{q_j}$, and $(\mathsf Du)_j=e^{\pi\alpha^2\beta_j^2}u_j$.

symbols.name: Gaussian diagonal
symbols.meaning: The diagonal map multiplying coordinate j by e^{pi alpha^2 beta_j^2}.
symbols.quote: Let $C$ select coordinates from length-$t$ to length-$s$ vectors, $(Cv)_j=v_{q_j}$, and $(\mathsf Du)_j=e^{\pi\alpha^2\beta_j^2}u_j$.

symbols.name: approximate identity
symbols.meaning: The map C T D on length-s vectors, close to the identity.

symbols.name: coordinate index
symbols.meaning: A single coordinate index of a vector, not an index tuple.
symbols.quote: Several letters are reused here with new meanings: $j$ and $k$ are single coordinate indices, not index tuples as in multidimensional transforms.

symbols.name: coordinate index
symbols.meaning: A single coordinate index of a vector, not an index tuple.
symbols.quote: Several letters are reused here with new meanings: $j$ and $k$ are single coordinate indices, not index tuples as in multidimensional transforms.

symbols.name: width parameter
symbols.meaning: An integer with 2<=alpha<sqrt p setting the width of the Gaussian weights.
symbols.quote: Let $s<t<2^p$ be coprime integers, where $p>100$ counts the fractional bits of each real and imaginary component, and let $\alpha$, the width parameter of the Gaussian weights below, be an integer with $2\le\alpha<\sqrt p$.

symbols.name: padded length
symbols.meaning: The nearby larger transform length, a power of two, into which the length-s transform is resampled.
symbols.quote: Gaussian resampling expresses a Fourier transform of length $s$ through one of a nearby larger length $t$ (a power of two there), so that only power-of-two transforms need a fast algorithm.
